title: Metropolis
why: Cinema's most influential city premiered in Berlin on 10 January 1927 — a film set in a future that keeps arriving.
alt: Caesar crosses the Rubicon, 10 January 49 BC

title: Fatal Assistance
why: Raoul Peck's film starts with the 35 seconds of the Haiti earthquake, 12 January 2010, and then follows the two years of failed help.

title: Casablanca
why: Warners rushed it into general release to land on the Casablanca Conference, which opened on 14 January 1943. The luckiest booking in Hollywood history.
alt: Marilyn Monroe marries Joe DiMaggio, 14 January 1954

title: Goodbye Christopher Robin
why: A.A. Milne was born on 18 January 1882; the film is what Winnie-the-Pooh cost his son.
alt: The Paris Peace Conference opens, 18 January 1919

title: Marie Antoinette
why: Louis XVI goes to the guillotine on 21 January 1793 in the Place de la Révolution.

title: Deepsea Challenge
why: Piccard and Walsh touch the floor of the Challenger Deep in the bathyscaphe Trieste on 23 January 1960 — the film's starting point and its rival.

title: The Charge of the Light Brigade
why: Victoria instituted the Victoria Cross on 29 January 1856, for the war this film tears apart.

title: Chaplin
why: Chaplin, Pickford, Fairbanks and Griffith founded United Artists on 5 February 1919 — the inmates taking over the asylum.

title: The Man Who Invented Christmas
why: Charles Dickens was born on 7 February 1812; this is the six weeks in which he wrote A Christmas Carol.
alt: The Beatles land at JFK, 7 February 1964 — A Hard Day's Night

title: A Town Like Alice
why: Singapore surrenders on 15 February 1942 and the women start walking.
alt: Paradise Road (1997); the USS Maine explodes, 15 February 1898

title: The Mummy
why: Howard Carter opened Tutankhamun's burial chamber on 16 February 1923, and Universal had a monster within a decade.

title: Giordano Bruno
why: Bruno is burned in the Campo de' Fiori on 17 February 1600 for saying the stars were suns.
alt: Madama Butterfly premieres at La Scala, 17 February 1904

title: Castles in the Sky
why: The Daventry Experiment of 26 February 1935 — Watson-Watt bounces a BBC signal off a bomber and invents radar.

title: The Lorax
why: Dr Seuss was born on 2 March 1904, which is why America reads aloud on this date.

title: Annie
why: Roosevelt is inaugurated on 4 March 1933 — 'the only thing we have to fear' — and the film puts Annie in the room for the New Deal.

title: Suffragette
why: International Women's Day, marked on 8 March since 1913.

title: Four Hours in My Lai
why: Charlie Company enters My Lai at 7:30am on 16 March 1968; the film reconstructs the next four hours from the men who were there.

title: A
why: Mori Tatsuya films Aum Shinrikyo from the inside after the sarin attack on the Tokyo subway, 20 March 1995.

title: Yesterday
why: Please Please Me, the album that starts everything, was released on 22 March 1963. This is the world where it wasn't.
alt: The Lumieres' first private projection, 22 March 1895

title: Vincere
why: Mussolini founds the Fasci Italiani di Combattimento in Milan on 23 March 1919, and starts erasing the wife who funded him.

title: Immortal Beloved
why: Opens with Beethoven's funeral — he died on 26 March 1827, and 20,000 Viennese followed the coffin.
alt: The Camp David Accords signed, 26 March 1979

title: Birdman
why: World Theatre Day, 27 March — and no film is more about what a stage does to a person.

title: Coming Home
why: The last American combat troops left Vietnam on 29 March 1973; this is what came back with them.

title: Sometimes in April
why: Date-stamps its way through the Rwandan genocide day by day; 7 April 1994 is when the roadblocks go up and the lists come out.

title: Sarafina!
why: Freedom Day: South Africa's first non-racial election, 27 April 1994 — the thing Sarafina's generation was jailed for.

title: Dien Bien Phu
why: The garrison falls on 7 May 1954 after 56 days — Schoendoerffer was there with a camera as a soldier.

title: The Cranes Are Flying
why: Ends on Victory Day, 9 May 1945, with Veronika handing out flowers to men who came back to somebody else.
alt: Come and See; Ballad of a Soldier

title: The Founder
why: The McDonald brothers open the San Bernardino drive-in on 15 May 1940 — the restaurant Ray Kroc takes off them.

title: Madras Cafe
why: Built around the assassination of Rajiv Gandhi at Sriperumbudur on the night of 21 May 1991.
alt: Lindbergh lands at Le Bourget, 21 May 1927 — The Spirit of St. Louis

title: The Private Life of Sherlock Holmes
why: Arthur Conan Doyle was born on 22 May 1859; Wilder's film is the most affectionate thing anyone has done to his creation.

title: The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy
why: Towel Day, 25 May — and the Earth is demolished on a Thursday, which is never a good day.
alt: Star Wars opens, 25 May 1977; JFK's moon pledge, 25 May 1961

title: Operation Finale
why: Adolf Eichmann is hanged at Ramla just before midnight on 31 May 1962 — the end of the operation the film stages.

title: Jubilee
why: Jarman's punk England is the Silver Jubilee of 7 June 1977 turned inside out — the same week the Sex Pistols played the Thames on a boat.
alt: The Filth and the Fury; The Great Rock 'n' Roll Swindle

title: Hearts and Minds
why: Nick Ut photographed Kim Phuc on Route 1 at Trang Bang on 8 June 1972; this is the film that put that war on trial.

title: Secretariat
why: The Belmont Stakes, 9 June 1973 — thirty-one lengths, and a track record nobody has touched since.

title: Escape from Alcatraz
why: Frank Morris and the Anglin brothers go up the ventilator shaft on the night of 11 June 1962 and are never seen again.

title: Grenfell
why: Steve McQueen's single, silent circling of the tower that burned on 14 June 2017.
alt: The Argentine surrender in the Falklands, 14 June 1982

title: The Young Victoria
why: They wake her at six on the morning of 20 June 1837 to tell her she is Queen.

title: The Big Lift
why: The Berlin Airlift begins on 26 June 1948 — shot in the ruins of Berlin with the men who actually flew it.
alt: Kennedy in Berlin, 26 June 1963; The UN Charter signed, 26 June 1945

title: 7 Days in Entebbe
why: Air France 139 is hijacked out of Athens on 27 June 1976; the raid comes a week later.
alt: Raid on Entebbe (1977); Victory at Entebbe

title: White Nights
why: Baryshnikov defected in Toronto on 29 June 1974; here he plays a dancer dragged back to the country he ran from.
alt: The first iPhone goes on sale, 29 June 2007
